The ZEPLIN-III experiment searching for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) operated in the Palmer Laboratory 1070 m underground (2850 m water equivalent) at the Boulby mine (North East of England) between 2006 and 2011.

lineage.quote: After 3 kg single phase ZEPLIN-I [1] and 31 kg double phase ZEPLIN-II [2] running between 2001 and 2006, ZEPLIN-III was the third generation of liquid xenon experiments deployed at Boulby.

physics_goals.quote: The detector measures both scintillation and ionisation produced by radiation interacting in the liquid to differentiate between the nuclear recoils expected from WIMPs and the electron recoil background signals
physics_goals.value: Search for WIMPs in a two-phase xenon TPC, discriminating nuclear from electron recoils by scintillation and ionisation

summary.plain: ZEPLIN-III was a 12 kg two-phase liquid xenon dark matter detector in the Boulby mine, the third and last of the ZEPLIN detectors, run from 2006 to 2011. It saw no dark matter and closed the ZEPLIN programme.
summary.technical: Two-phase xenon TPC with 12 kg of liquid xenon in the Palmer Laboratory (1070 m, 2850 m.w.e.). First science run 27 Feb - 20 May 2008 (83 days) gave a spin-independent limit of 8.1e-8 pb at 55 GeV/c^2; after an upgrade (low-background PMTs, plastic-scintillator veto) the second run (24 Jun 2010 - 7 May 2011, 319 days, 1344 kg d raw) gave 4.8e-8 pb near 50 GeV/c^2 (3.9e-8 pb combined).
